name: AI Strategy Planner
tag: Maps your workflows, picks where AI helps most, generates the MCP servers to connect your tools and estimates the return.

scenarios.title: Find the best AI opportunities
scenarios.ask: Assess our {workflows} main workflows. We have {staff} staff at about ${rate} an hour.
steps: Interviewer
Asked short questions about each of the {workflows} workflows: steps, tools, volume and errors.
Scorer
Rated each on time spent, repetition and risk. {=max(1, round(workflows * 0.3))} scored high for AI help.
Strategist
Grouped them into a 3-phase roadmap: quick wins, connected tools, then agents.
ROI model
Estimated about {=round(staff * 2.5)} staff hours a week freed in phase one.
followups: Where do the hour estimates come from?
From your own answers about volume and time per task, cut by a safety margin. They're estimates to rank options, not promises.
Usually a document or email task done many times a day, because it's easy to measure and low risk.

scenarios.title: Connect our tools with MCP
scenarios.ask: Generate MCP servers so our AI assistant can use {tools} of our business tools, with {access} access.
steps: Tool mapper
Listed what each of the {tools} tools can do through its API and what your team actually uses.
Generator
Wrote {tools} MCP servers exposing about {=tools * (3 + access * 2)} actions in total.
Guardrails
Set {access} access, with every write action held for a person to approve.
Tester
Ran sample requests against each server using test accounts.
followups: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for letting AI assistants use tools and data. Each server is a small connector to one tool.
Is read-only enough to be useful?
Often, yes. Letting the assistant look things up across tools saves time on its own, and you can add write actions later.

scenarios.title: Build the business case
scenarios.ask: Our board wants a business case for a ${budget} AI program. Show payback.
steps: ROI model
Year-one value: {hours} a week at ${rate} for 48 weeks is ${=hours * rate * 48}.
Risk adjuster
Applied a 30% haircut for slow adoption, giving ${=round(hours * rate * 48 * 0.7)}.
Writer
Drafted a 2-page case with scope, costs, risks and how success is measured.
Reviewer
Listed questions a board is likely to ask, with answers.
followups: At half the expected hours, payback stretches to about {=round(budget / max(1, hours * rate * 2 * 0.7), 1)} months. The case shows both lines.
Pick two or three tracked numbers, such as handling time per request, before you start. The plan reports them monthly.
